listings.commonName: Burmese Cloud Archerfish (Toxotes blythii)
listings.description: Species Overview The Burmese Cloud Archerfish ( Toxotes blythii ) is one of the rarest and most fascinating freshwater fish available in the aquarium hobby. Native to the rivers and streams of Myanmar, this remarkable species is best known for the incredible hunting behavior that has made archerfish famous around the world. Using carefully aimed jets of water, Burmese Cloud Archerfish can knock insects and other prey from overhanging vegetation before quickly capturing them at the water's surface. Combined with their striking silver body and bold cloud-like markings, this unique behavior makes them an unforgettable centerpiece for a large freshwater aquarium. Unlike many commonly available archerfish, Burmese Cloud Archerfish are primarily a freshwater species and thrive in spacious aquariums with excellent water quality, open swimming areas, and a varied carnivorous diet. They are intelligent, curious fish that quickly learn feeding routines and often become one of the most interactive inhabitants in the aquarium. Because they grow considerably larger than their juvenile purchase size and have a naturally predatory appetite, they are best suited for experienced aquarists who can provide appropriately sized tank mates and ample swimming space. Every Burmese Cloud Archerfish at Aquatic Arts is carefully quarantined, observed, and conditioned before shipment to help ensure it arrives healthy and ready to thrive. For aquarists seeking a truly uncommon species with remarkable natural behaviors, the Burmese Cloud Archerfish offers a rewarding fishkeeping experience unlike almost any other freshwater fish. What We Love About Burmese Cloud Archerfish One of the rarest freshwater archerfish available in the aquarium hobby. Famous for their remarkable ability to shoot jets of water at insect prey. Beautiful silver body with distinctive dark cloud-like markings. Highly intelligent and interactive with their keeper. Active surface-dwelling fish that provide constant movement. Excellent centerpiece fish for large freshwater community aquariums. Primarily a freshwater species, unlike many commonly available archerfish. A fascinating choice for aquarists looking for a truly unique display fish. Recommended Water Parameters & Aquarium Requirements Burmese Cloud Archerfish naturally inhabit warm, slow to moderately flowing freshwater rivers and streams throughout Myanmar. They thrive in stable, well-maintained aquariums that provide excellent water quality, ample swimming space, and a secure environment. Consistency is far more important than chasing exact numbers. Water Parameters Temperature: 74–82°F (23–28°C). Warm, stable temperatures support healthy metabolism, activity, and long-term health. pH: 6.8–7.8. Burmese Cloud Archerfish adapt well to neutral and slightly alkaline freshwater when water chemistry remains stable. General Hardness (GH): 5–15 dGH. Moderate hardness closely matches much of their natural habitat. Carbonate Hardness (KH): 3–10 dKH. Adequate buffering helps prevent sudden pH swings. Ammonia: 0 ppm. Always maintain undetectable ammonia. Nitrite: 0 ppm. Nitrite should always remain at zero. Nitrate: Below 20 ppm (under 10 ppm preferred). Regular maintenance helps maintain optimal long-term health. Aquarium Requirements Minimum Aquarium Size: 125 gallons. Burmese Cloud Archerfish become large, active fish that require significant horizontal swimming space throughout their lives. Aquarium Length: At least 6 feet (180 cm) recommended. A longer aquarium is more beneficial than a taller one because this species spends much of its time cruising the upper water column. Filtration: High-quality biological and mechanical filtration. As large carnivorous fish, Burmese Cloud Archerfish produce a moderate biological load and benefit from efficient filtration and consistent maintenance. Water Flow: Gentle to Moderate. Moderate circulation helps maintain oxygen levels without creating excessive surface turbulence. Aquascape: Open swimming areas with driftwood, branches, floating plants, and shaded areas. These features mimic their natural habitat while leaving plenty of room for active swimming. Lighting: Moderate. Bright lighting can be softened with floating plants or overhanging hardscape to create a more natural environment. Aquarium Lid: A secure, tight-fitting lid is essential. Burmese Cloud Archerfish are powerful surface-oriented fish that may jump when startled or while pursuing food. Aquarium Maturity: Well-established aquarium recommended. Stable biological filtration and consistent water chemistry are important for long-term success. Aquatic Arts Tips Burmese Cloud Archerfish are intelligent, active fish that appreciate a thoughtfully designed aquarium. Prioritize swimming space over excessive decorations, maintain excellent water quality through regular maintenance, and always keep the aquarium securely covered. Providing floating vegetation or overhanging branches can encourage more natural surface-oriented behaviors while creating an attractive, river-inspired display.

listings.commonName: L236 Cracked Zebra Pleco (Hypancistrus sp.) – Tank-Bred
listings.description: Species Overview The Cracked Zebra Pleco ( Hypancistrus sp. L236) is one of the most sought-after members of the Hypancistrus genus, admired for its intricate black-and-white pattern that resembles cracked porcelain or fractured zebra striping. Native to the Xingu River basin in Brazil, this beautiful dwarf pleco has become increasingly popular among aquarists who appreciate rare Loricariid catfish with distinctive markings, manageable adult sizes, and fascinating cave-spawning behavior. Every Cracked Zebra Pleco develops its own unique pattern, making each fish a truly one-of-a-kind addition to the aquarium. Known for their peaceful temperament and relatively small adult size, Cracked Zebra Plecos thrive in mature aquariums with warm, highly oxygenated water, excellent filtration, and plenty of caves and driftwood. They spend much of the day tucked beneath cover before becoming increasingly active during the evening hours, grazing on biofilm and searching for meaty foods. Their calm disposition makes them an excellent choice for peaceful community aquariums and dedicated pleco collections alike. Aquatic Arts is proud to offer tank-bred Cracked Zebra Plecos, including USA-bred specimens when available. Tank-bred fish are generally well adapted to aquarium life, helping hobbyists enjoy healthy, established fish while supporting the continued growth of captive breeding efforts. Whether you're purchasing your first L-number pleco or adding another rare Hypancistrus species to your collection, the Cracked Zebra Pleco offers exceptional beauty, personality, and long-term reward. What We Love About L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos Beautiful maze-like black-and-white pattern that makes every L236 Cracked Zebra Pleco unique. Tank-bred fish that are well acclimated to aquarium life and help support sustainable captive breeding. Peaceful temperament that makes L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos excellent additions to carefully planned community aquariums. Manageable adult size compared to many larger pleco species. Fascinating cave-spawning behavior that has made the L236 Cracked Zebra Pleco a favorite among pleco breeders. Primarily nocturnal, becoming increasingly active during the evening as they forage for food. Excellent choice for dedicated Hypancistrus collections and South American aquarium displays. Long-lived fish that reward patient aquarists with years of enjoyment when provided proper care. Scientific Name: Hypancistrus sp. L236 Common Name: L236 Cracked Zebra Pleco Source: USA Bred or Tank-Bred (Varies by Selection) Average Purchase Size: Approximately 1–1.25 inches. Juvenile L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos adapt well to established aquariums and allow hobbyists to enjoy watching their pattern develop as they mature. Average Adult Size: Approximately 4.5–5 inches (11–13 cm). L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos remain a manageable size, making them an excellent choice for aquarists seeking a rare pleco without the space requirements of many larger Loricariids. Care Level: Moderate. L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos thrive in mature aquariums with excellent water quality, high dissolved oxygen, warm temperatures, and plenty of secure caves and hiding places. Temperament: Peaceful. L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos are non-aggressive toward most community fish and other peaceful bottom dwellers but may establish territories around preferred caves, especially during breeding. Diet: Omnivore with a Carnivorous Preference. Feed a varied diet of high-quality sinking carnivore pellets, Repashy gel foods, frozen foods, live foods, and occasional vegetable-based foods to support healthy growth and coloration. Social Behavior: Solitary to Loose Groups. L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos can be kept individually or in groups when sufficient caves and territory are provided. Multiple individuals generally coexist well when competition for shelter is minimized. Activity Level: Mostly Nocturnal. L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos spend much of the day inside caves or beneath driftwood before becoming increasingly active during the evening and overnight hours. Aquarium Level: Bottom Dweller. L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos spend nearly all of their time exploring caves, driftwood, and rocky structures along the aquarium floor. Minimum Aquarium Size: 30 Gallons. A mature aquarium with abundant hiding places and stable water quality is more important than tank size alone, although larger aquariums are recommended for groups or breeding projects. Lifespan: Approximately 10–15 Years with proper care, making the L236 Cracked Zebra Pleco a rewarding long-term addition to a peaceful freshwater aquarium. Recommended Water Parameters & Aquarium Requirements L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos originate from warm, fast-flowing South American rivers where the water is exceptionally clean, highly oxygenated, and rich in dissolved minerals. Replicating these stable conditions is one of the most important factors in successfully keeping and breeding this beautiful Hypancistrus species. Excellent filtration, strong oxygenation, and consistent maintenance are more important than chasing exact water parameters. Water Parameters Temperature: 80–86°F (27–30°C). L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos thrive in warmer water that closely resembles their native habitat and supports healthy metabolism and breeding activity. pH: 6.2–7.4. Slightly acidic to neutral water is ideal, although stability is more important than achieving a specific pH. General Hardness (GH): 2–10 dGH. Soft to moderately hard water closely reflects the mineral content found throughout much of their natural range. Carbonate Hardness (KH): 1–5 dKH. Moderate buffering helps maintain stable water chemistry without excessive hardness. Ammonia: 0 ppm. Ammonia is highly toxic and should never be detectable in a healthy aquarium. Nitrite: 0 ppm. Nitrite should always remain undetectable. Nitrate: Below 20 ppm (under 10 ppm preferred). Regular water changes help maintain excellent water quality and encourage healthy long-term growth and breeding. Aquarium Requirements Minimum Aquarium Size: 30 Gallons. A mature aquarium is suitable for a single L236 Cracked Zebra Pleco, while larger aquariums provide additional territory for multiple fish or breeding groups. Filtration: High-quality biological filtration with strong water movement. L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos naturally inhabit highly oxygenated rivers and benefit from excellent circulation and clean water. Water Flow: Moderate to Strong. Good current helps increase dissolved oxygen while recreating the river environments these plecos naturally inhabit. Oxygenation: High. Additional surface agitation or air stones are beneficial, especially in warmer aquariums where oxygen levels naturally decrease. Aquarium Maturity: A well-established aquarium is strongly recommended. Mature biological filtration and stable water chemistry are essential for the long-term health of L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos. Hiding Places: Provide multiple caves and secure shelters. Ceramic breeding caves, slate caves, rock crevices, and driftwood allow L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos to establish territories, reduce stress, and encourage natural behavior. Lighting: Low to Moderate. Bright lighting is acceptable when broken up with driftwood, caves, and shaded areas that allow the fish to retreat during the day. Aquatic Arts Tip L236 Cracked Zebra Plecos are far more sensitive to declining water quality than many common plecos. Clean, highly oxygenated water, abundant caves, and consistent weekly maintenance will do more for their long-term health and breeding success than constantly adjusting water chemistry. Focus on stability, excellent filtration, and providing numerous secure hiding places, and these beautiful plecos will reward you with natural behaviors and vibrant condition.

listings.commonName: Lagos Red Killifish (Aphyosemion bivittatum "Lagos") - Tank Bred
listings.description: Species Description The Lagos Red Killifish ( Aphyosemion bivittatum "Lagos") is a beautifully patterned West African killifish known for its slender, elongated body, distinctive horizontal striping, and combination of red, blue-green, yellow, and orange coloration. The "Lagos" designation refers to the geographic locality associated with this form in Nigeria rather than simply describing its coloration. Mature males develop the most intense colors, with two characteristic dark horizontal bands accented by iridescent blue-green tones, red patterning, and yellow to orange highlights, while females display a more subdued pattern and fuller body shape. This species may also be encountered in the killifish hobby as Chromaphyosemion bivittatum under an alternative taxonomic treatment. It should not be confused with the commonly available Gardner's Killifish ( Fundulopanchax gardneri ), which is a different species. Lagos Red Killifish are also non-annual killifish , meaning their natural reproductive cycle does not require the prolonged dry egg-incubation period associated with many annual African killifish. Our Lagos Red Killifish are tank bred and offer something genuinely different for aquarists interested in West African killifish, planted aquariums, and locality-associated strains. Their manageable size, beautiful male coloration, interesting breeding behavior, and distinctive appearance make them especially rewarding for hobbyists looking to move beyond the more commonly available killifish species. What We Love About This Fish Beautiful two-banded pattern accented by red, blue-green, yellow, and orange coloration, particularly in mature males. A genuine West African locality-associated killifish that offers something different from the more commonly available Fundulopanchax gardneri . Non-annual breeding biology makes reproduction approachable without the prolonged dry egg incubation associated with annual killifish. Tank bred for aquarium life and an especially rewarding choice for planted species-focused and carefully planned community aquariums. Quick Care Guide Care Level: Intermediate. Lagos Red Killifish are manageable for aquarists familiar with maintaining stable water conditions, but they deserve more specialized care than many common beginner community fish. Temperament: Generally peaceful, with some territorial behavior possible between males. Plants, wood, and other visual barriers help provide individual territories and reduce persistent chasing. Diet: Carnivore/Insectivore. Small live and frozen foods are particularly valuable, although tank-bred specimens may also accept appropriately sized high-quality prepared foods. Source: Tank Bred. Average Adult Size: Approximately 2 inches (5 cm). Suggested Minimum Aquarium Size: 10 gallons for a pair or carefully managed small group, with additional space recommended when maintaining multiple males or a community. Swimming Zone: Primarily upper to middle water column. Activity Level: Moderately active. Lagos Red Killifish spend considerable time exploring vegetation, investigating potential food, and interacting with other members of their species. Social Behavior: Pairs or small groups can be maintained with sufficient structure and cover. Multiple males require enough room and broken sight lines to establish space without constant confrontation. Breeding: Egg layer and non-annual killifish. Eggs are deposited among fine vegetation, plant roots, or spawning mops rather than requiring a seasonal dry period. Approximate Purchase Size: Young fish may arrive before developing their full adult coloration. Male coloration and finnage become considerably more impressive with maturity. Important: A secure, tightly fitted lid is strongly recommended. Killifish are accomplished jumpers and can escape through surprisingly small openings. Water Parameters Temperature: 68°–75°F (20°–24°C). Lagos Red Killifish generally appreciate cooler tropical conditions rather than the consistently high temperatures used for many warm-water community species. pH: Approximately 6.0–7.5. Slightly acidic to near-neutral conditions are a good target, with stability more important than chasing an exact number. General Hardness (GH): Soft to moderately hard water is appropriate. Avoid sudden changes in mineral content. Carbonate Hardness (KH): Low to moderate carbonate hardness is suitable provided the aquarium maintains a stable pH. Clean water, consistent parameters, and regular partial water changes are especially important. As with many killifish, maintaining good water quality is more valuable than continually adjusting the aquarium in pursuit of a single "perfect" parameter.

listings.commonName: Figure 8 Puffer (Dichotomyctere ocellatus)
listings.description: Species Overview The Figure 8 Puffer ( Dichotomyctere ocellatus ) is one of the most recognizable small puffers in the aquarium hobby, named for the looping black markings across its back that often resemble the number eight. Its bright yellow-green coloration, bold patterning, constantly moving eyes, and unusual swimming style give this fish an incredible amount of personality for its size. You may also recognize this species by its older scientific name, Tetraodon biocellatus , which is still commonly used throughout the aquarium trade. What really makes the Figure 8 Puffer special, though, is its behavior. These are intelligent, curious fish that spend much of the day inspecting rocks, wood, substrate, and anything else that changes within their environment. Many quickly learn where food comes from and will begin following their keeper along the aquarium glass at feeding time. It's difficult to keep one for very long without beginning to recognize its individual habits and personality. The Figure 8 Puffer is best suited to an aquarist who wants to build an aquarium around the needs of the fish rather than simply add another species to an existing community. Proper salinity, excellent water quality, a thoughtfully structured environment, and a diet that includes hard-shelled foods are important parts of long-term care. For the aquarist willing to provide those things, few freshwater or brackish aquarium fish offer quite the same combination of intelligence, curiosity, and personality. What We Love About This Fish Huge personality in a small fish – Figure 8 Puffers are intelligent, observant, and constantly investigating their surroundings. Unmistakable patterning – Yellow-green coloration and looping black markings give every Figure 8 Puffer a slightly different appearance. Fascinating feeding behavior – Watching a Figure 8 Puffer hunt snails, crustaceans, and other hard-shelled foods is one of the most interesting parts of keeping the species. Quick Care Guide Care Level: Intermediate Temperament: Semi-Aggressive; may be territorial and prone to fin-nipping Diet: Carnivorous; snails, crustaceans, mollusks, frozen foods, and other meaty foods Source: Collected Average Adult Size: Approximately 3 inches (7.5 cm) Average Purchase Size: Approximately 1–2 inches (2.5–5 cm) Minimum Aquarium Size: 20 gallons for a single adult; additional space is required when attempting to maintain more than one Tank Level: All Levels Activity Level: Active Social Classification: Best maintained individually or in a carefully planned species-focused aquarium Shrimp Safe: No Plant Safe: Generally, although brackish conditions significantly limit suitable plant choices Special Requirement: Hard-shelled foods should be included regularly to help manage continuously growing teeth Recommended Water Parameters Temperature: 75–82°F (24–28°C) pH: 7.0–8.0 General Hardness (GH): 8–20 dGH Carbonate Hardness (KH): 6–15 dKH Salinity: Fresh to low-end brackish; stable low-end brackish conditions are commonly recommended for long-term aquarium care Specific Gravity: Approximately 1.002–1.005 when maintained as a low-end brackish aquarium A Note About Freshwater vs. Brackish Water This is one of the most confusing parts of Figure 8 Puffer care because you'll find them described online as both freshwater and brackish fish. There is a reason for that. Dichotomyctere ocellatus occurs naturally in environments influenced by both fresh and brackish water, and specimens can tolerate a range of salinities. For long-term aquarium care, we recommend maintaining Figure 8 Puffers in stable low-end brackish conditions rather than treating them as conventional freshwater community fish. Marine salt mix should be used to create brackish water, and salinity should be measured rather than estimated by simply adding aquarium salt. Stability and water quality matter more than constantly changing salinity in an attempt to imitate tidal conditions. Figure 8 Puffers are also messy eaters and are sensitive to deteriorating water quality. Strong biological filtration, good oxygenation, regular water changes, and a fully cycled aquarium are especially important. Their relatively small adult size should never be mistaken for low waste production or low maintenance.

listings.commonName: Red Glass Barb (Pethia conchonius) – Tank-Bred
listings.description: Species Overview The Red Glass Barb ( Pethia conchonius ) is a colorful, active freshwater barb prized for its translucent appearance and warm red to rosy coloration. Closely associated with the familiar Rosy Barb, this selectively bred aquarium form combines the energetic schooling behavior that makes barbs so enjoyable to watch with a distinctive lighter-bodied appearance that allows flashes of red, silver, and iridescence to stand out as the fish move through the aquarium. Mature males generally develop the strongest coloration, particularly when comfortable and displaying among other members of their group. Red Glass Barbs are social fish and should be maintained in a proper group rather than as solitary specimens. When given sufficient swimming room, plant cover, and the company of their own kind, the group creates constant movement throughout the middle levels of the aquarium. Their adaptability, enthusiastic feeding response, and compatibility with many appropriately chosen community fish make them an excellent option for aquarists looking for an active schooling species rather than a single centerpiece fish. Aquatic Arts offers Tank-Bred and USA-Bred Red Glass Barbs , depending on the selection purchased. Captive-bred Red Glass Barbs are accustomed to aquarium conditions and prepared foods, making them an excellent choice for established freshwater community aquariums. What We Love About This Fish Beautiful red glass coloration combines warm red tones with a lighter, partially translucent body that becomes especially striking as a group moves through a planted aquarium. True social behavior makes a properly sized group considerably more interesting to watch than a single fish, with schooling, displaying, and constant interaction between individuals. Tank-Bred and USA-Bred selections give customers the opportunity to choose captive-bred fish based on their preferred source. Active without requiring an enormous aquarium , making Red Glass Barbs an excellent way to add movement and color to a thoughtfully planned community setup. Hardy and adaptable aquarium fish that readily accept a varied diet and can be an approachable choice for aquarists ready to maintain an appropriate social group. Quick Care Guide Scientific Name: Pethia conchonius Common Name: Red Glass Barb Source: Tank-Bred or USA Bred (Varies by Selection) Average Purchase Size: Approximately 1–1.5 Inches (2.5–3.8 cm) Average Adult Size: Approximately 4–6 Inches (10–15 cm), so considerably more swimming space is needed as these active barbs mature. Care Level: Easy to Moderate. Red Glass Barbs are hardy and adaptable but require clean water, open swimming space, and a proper social group. Temperament: Peaceful to Semi-Peaceful. They generally make excellent community fish but may occasionally nip slow-moving or long-finned tank mates. Diet: Omnivore. A varied diet of quality prepared, frozen, live, and plant-based foods supports healthy growth and strong coloration. Schooling: Yes. Red Glass Barbs should be kept in a group so they can display natural social behavior and distribute chasing among the school. Activity Level: Active. These energetic barbs need plenty of open horizontal swimming space. Aquarium Level: Midwater. Red Glass Barbs spend most of their time actively swimming through the middle of the aquarium. Minimum Aquarium Size: 30 Gallons. Their adult size, activity level, and schooling behavior require more room than their juvenile purchase size suggests. Lifespan: Approximately 5–7 Years with proper care. Aquatic Arts Tip Plan the aquarium around the adult school , not the size of the juveniles you receive. Give Red Glass Barbs plenty of open swimming room surrounded by planted areas where the group can retreat and feel secure. Recommended Water Parameters & Aquarium Requirements Red Glass Barbs are adaptable fish, but they thrive when given stable water conditions, good filtration, and plenty of swimming room for their active school. Water Parameters Temperature: 64–75°F (18–24°C). Red Glass Barbs prefer cooler conditions than many tropical community fish. pH: 6.5–7.5. Red Glass Barbs thrive in slightly acidic to slightly alkaline water, with stability being more important than targeting an exact number. General Hardness (GH): 4–18 dGH. Soft to moderately hard water is generally well tolerated. Carbonate Hardness (KH): 2–12 dKH. Stable buffering helps prevent sudden changes in pH. Ammonia: 0 ppm Nitrite: 0 ppm Nitrate: Below 20 ppm preferred. Aquarium Requirements Minimum Aquarium Size: 30 Gallons. Their adult size and active schooling behavior require plenty of horizontal swimming room. Filtration: Moderate to Strong. Good filtration helps maintain the clean, oxygen-rich water these active fish prefer. Water Flow: Moderate. Red Glass Barbs appreciate water movement but should also have calmer areas for resting. Oxygenation: Moderate to High. Good surface agitation supports the active metabolism of the school. Aquarium Maturity: Fully cycled and established. Stable biological filtration reduces the risk of sudden water-quality problems. Aquatic Plants: Recommended. Planting around the sides and back provides security while preserving an open central swimming area. Lighting: Low to Moderate. Moderate lighting works well, especially when balanced with live plants and shaded areas. Aquatic Arts Tip Give Red Glass Barbs a combination of open swimming space and planted cover rather than filling the entire aquarium with décor. This gives the school room to move while still providing secure areas where fish can retreat when needed.

listings.commonName: Longfin Zebra Danio (Danio rerio) – Tank-Bred
listings.description: Species Overview The Longfin Zebra Danio ( Danio rerio ) combines the familiar striped pattern and energetic personality of the classic Zebra Danio with dramatically extended fins that create extra movement as the fish swims. Alternating blue-black and metallic silver-gold horizontal stripes run along the body, while the elongated fins give this selectively bred form a noticeably more graceful appearance than the standard-fin Zebra Danio. Longfin Zebra Danios are hardy, active schooling fish that spend much of the day swimming and interacting with one another. Their adaptability and willingness to accept a wide variety of foods make them an approachable choice for newer aquarists, while their constant activity and flowing fins give established community aquariums plenty of visual interest. Aquatic Arts offers both Tank-Bred and USA Bred Longfin Zebra Danios , depending on the selection purchased. What We Love About This Fish Long, flowing fins transform the familiar Zebra Danio into a more dramatic display fish while retaining its characteristic striped pattern. Active schooling behavior creates constant movement as the fish swim, chase, and interact throughout the aquarium. Hardy and adaptable , making Longfin Zebra Danios an excellent choice for newer aquarists as well as established community aquariums. Tank-Bred and USA Bred selections provide customers with a choice of captive-bred sources. Excellent planted-community fish that brings movement to open swimming areas while contrasting beautifully against live plants and natural hardscape. Quick Care Guide Scientific Name: Danio rerio Common Name: Longfin Zebra Danio Source: Tank-Bred or USA Bred (Varies by Selection) Average Purchase Size: Approximately 1–1.5 Inches (2.5–3.8 cm) Average Adult Size: Approximately 2–2.5 Inches (5–6.4 cm), making Longfin Zebra Danios small fish that still need plenty of swimming room due to their activity level. Care Level: Easy. Longfin Zebra Danios are hardy and adaptable when maintained in a fully cycled aquarium with stable water quality. Temperament: Peaceful and Active. Their energetic behavior works best with similarly active community fish that will not be overwhelmed by a fast-moving school. Diet: Omnivore. A varied diet of quality prepared, frozen, and live foods supports healthy growth, coloration, and activity. Schooling: Yes. Longfin Zebra Danios should be maintained in a group so they can display natural schooling and social behavior. Activity Level: Very Active. These energetic fish need plenty of open horizontal swimming space despite their relatively small adult size. Aquarium Level: Upper to Midwater. Longfin Zebra Danios spend much of the day actively swimming through the upper half of the aquarium. Minimum Aquarium Size: 20 Gallons Long. Horizontal swimming space is particularly important for an active school of Longfin Zebra Danios. Lifespan: Approximately 3–5 Years with proper care. Lid Requirement: Secure Lid Recommended. Longfin Zebra Danios are active swimmers and capable jumpers, especially when startled. Aquatic Arts Tip Think about swimming length rather than gallons alone when choosing an aquarium for Longfin Zebra Danios. A longer aquarium gives the school room to move naturally while planted areas along the sides and back provide places to retreat when needed. Tank Requirements Longfin Zebra Danios are adaptable fish that thrive in clean, stable water with good oxygenation and plenty of open swimming space. Their active schooling behavior makes aquarium length and water quality especially important. Water Parameters Temperature: 65–75°F (18–24°C). Longfin Zebra Danios prefer slightly cooler conditions than many tropical community fish. pH: 6.5–7.5. Slightly acidic to slightly alkaline water works well when conditions remain stable. General Hardness (GH): 5–15 dGH. Soft to moderately hard water is well suited to this adaptable species. Carbonate Hardness (KH): 3–10 dKH. Moderate buffering helps maintain stable water chemistry. Ammonia: 0 ppm Nitrite: 0 ppm Nitrate: Below 20 ppm preferred. Aquarium Requirements Minimum Aquarium Size: 20 Gallons Long. The longer footprint provides valuable horizontal swimming room for an active school. Filtration: Moderate. Reliable biological filtration keeps the water clean while providing gentle circulation. Water Flow: Moderate. Longfin Zebra Danios enjoy moving water but should also have calmer areas where their extended fins are not constantly fighting the current. Oxygenation: Moderate to High. Good surface agitation helps maintain the oxygen-rich conditions these active fish prefer. Aquarium Maturity: Fully cycled and established. Stable biological filtration protects the school from sudden changes in water quality. Aquatic Plants: Recommended. Plants around the perimeter provide security while preserving open swimming space through the center. Lighting: Low to Moderate. Standard aquarium lighting works well, particularly when balanced with planted or shaded areas. Aquatic Arts Tip Longfin Zebra Danios have the same energetic nature as standard Zebra Danios but considerably more finnage. Provide good circulation without excessive current so the fish receive excellent oxygenation while still having areas where they can swim comfortably without their long fins working against strong flow.

listings.commonName: Tennyo no Mai Medaka (Oryzias latipes) – Tank-Bred
listings.description: Species Overview The Tennyo no Mai Medaka ( Oryzias latipes ) , also known as the Heavenly Maiden Dance Ricefish , is a striking long-finned Japanese Ricefish developed by combining the Matsui long-fin trait with a Miyuki base. The result brings together the reflective, metallic appearance associated with Miyuki Medaka and dramatically elongated finnage that gives mature Tennyo no Mai their characteristic flowing appearance. The name Tennyo no Mai (天女の舞) translates approximately to “Dance of the Heavenly Maiden,” inspired by the graceful movement of the fish's extended fins as it swims. Unlike standard-finned Miyuki Medaka, the fins of Tennyo no Mai become increasingly prominent as the fish matures, so younger specimens may not yet display the dramatic finnage seen in fully developed adults. Individual fish can also vary naturally in fin length, body sheen, and overall expression. Despite its elaborate appearance, Tennyo no Mai retains the active, social nature that makes Japanese Ricefish so enjoyable to keep. These tank-bred Medaka spend much of their time near the upper levels of the aquarium and can be kept in planted aquariums, dedicated Medaka displays, and appropriately managed outdoor container setups. Their combination of metallic coloration, flowing finnage, manageable adult size, and peaceful behavior makes Tennyo no Mai a particularly distinctive expression of Oryzias latipes . What We Love About This Fish Flowing Long-Fin Form: The Matsui long-fin trait gives mature Tennyo no Mai their signature extended finnage and graceful movement. Miyuki Metallic Sheen: Their Miyuki heritage contributes the bright silver to blue-white reflective appearance that makes these Medaka beautiful from above or from the side. Gets Better With Maturity: The characteristic finnage continues to develop as Tennyo no Mai grow, making this an especially rewarding variety to raise to adulthood. Peaceful and Social: Their small size and generally peaceful behavior make Tennyo no Mai well suited to planted Medaka displays and carefully selected community aquariums. Quick Care Guide Care Level: Easy to Moderate — Tennyo no Mai Medaka retain the adaptability of Japanese Ricefish, but their elongated fins make clean water, gentle flow, and appropriate tank mates especially important. Temperament: Peaceful — Tennyo no Mai are generally peaceful toward their own kind and other appropriately selected community fish. Diet: Omnivore — Offer a varied diet of high-quality small pellets or flakes along with appropriately sized live and frozen foods such as Daphnia, Moina, and Baby Brine Shrimp. Average Adult Size: 1.25–1.5 inches (3–4 cm) — Their elongated fins can make mature Tennyo no Mai appear larger than standard-finned Medaka of the same body size. Average Purchase Size: Approximately 1–1.5 inches Tank Level: Upper to Middle — Like other Japanese Ricefish, Tennyo no Mai spend much of their time swimming and feeding near the water's surface. Activity Level: Active — These curious ricefish regularly explore open water and planted areas throughout the day. Social Behavior: Social — Tennyo no Mai should be kept with other Medaka rather than as solitary fish, with enough space for individuals to interact without crowding. Shrimp Compatibility: Yes, with adult shrimp — Adult freshwater shrimp are generally safe, although very small shrimplets may be eaten opportunistically. Tank Parameters Minimum Tank Size: 10 gallons — A 10-gallon aquarium provides adequate space for a small group, although larger footprints offer more swimming room and greater water stability. Temperature: 64–78°F (18–26°C) — Tennyo no Mai Medaka are temperate fish and do not require the consistently warm conditions needed by many tropical species. pH: 6.5–8.0 — Japanese Ricefish are adaptable to a relatively broad pH range, but stable conditions are more important than trying to maintain a specific number within that range. GH: 5–20 dGH — Tennyo no Mai tolerate a broad range of mineral content and generally do well in moderately soft to hard water. KH: 2–12 dKH — Some carbonate hardness helps provide buffering and reduces the likelihood of sudden pH changes. Water Flow: Gentle to Moderate — Good filtration and oxygenation are important, but Tennyo no Mai should not have to constantly fight strong current with their elongated fins. Aquarium Cover: Secure lid recommended — Medaka spend considerable time near the surface and are capable jumpers, particularly when startled or during active social interactions.

listings.commonName: Freshwater Live Food Variety Pack – Blackworms & Bladder Snails
listings.description: PRODUCT DESCRIPTION The Freshwater Live Food Variety Pack – Blackworms & Bladder Snails brings together two very different live foods for freshwater fish that naturally hunt, forage, and search for aquatic invertebrates. Live Blackworms provide soft-bodied, moving food that many carnivorous and omnivorous fish readily pursue, while Bladder Snails give snail-eating species an opportunity to locate and work at live shelled food. This combination is particularly useful for Pea Puffers and other pufferfish that eat appropriately sized snails and worms , as well as snail-eating loaches and other freshwater fish that benefit from live-food variety. Rather than simply providing two flavors of the same type of food, Blackworms and Bladder Snails encourage distinctly different feeding behaviors. Each pack includes your choice of a 2 oz or 4 oz portion of USA-Bred Live Blackworms , along with 20+ Bladder Snails Bred by Aquatic Arts . The snails can be fed as needed or used to help establish a separate feeder-snail colony for aquarists who want an ongoing source of appropriately sized live snails. Live foods do not need to replace a balanced prepared or frozen diet. Instead, they can add dietary variety, encourage natural feeding and foraging behaviors, and provide another useful feeding option for breeders and aquarists keeping fish that respond particularly well to moving foods. WHAT WE LOVE ABOUT THIS LIVE FOOD VARIETY PACK Two Different Feeding Experiences: Moving Blackworms and live snails encourage different hunting and foraging behaviors. Excellent Puffer Food Combination: Especially useful for Pea Puffers and other appropriately sized snail- and worm-eating puffers. More Than One Meal: Bladder Snails can be maintained separately to establish a renewable feeder colony. Know Where Your Food Comes From: Blackworms are USA-bred, while the Bladder Snails are bred right here at Aquatic Arts. PACK OPTIONS 2 oz Live Blackworms + 20+ Bladder Snails 4 oz Live Blackworms + 20+ Bladder Snails QUICK CARE / FEEDING GUIDE Product Type: Live Freshwater Food Variety Pack Includes: Live Blackworms + Live Bladder Snails Blackworm Portion: Choice of 2 oz or 4 oz Bladder Snail Portion: 20+ count Blackworm Source: USA-Bred Bladder Snail Source: Bred by Aquatic Arts Best For: Freshwater puffers, snail-eating loaches, and other carnivorous or omnivorous fish that consume live aquatic invertebrates Feeding Use: Supplemental live food, feeding enrichment, conditioning, and natural foraging opportunities Feeding Amount: Offer only what is appropriate for the number and size of fish being fed. The entire portion is not intended to be fed at once. Bladder Snail Culture: Extra snails can be maintained separately and allowed to reproduce for an ongoing supply of live feeder snails Water Type: Freshwater

listings.commonName: Freshwater Live Food Variety Pack – Fry and Micro Foods
listings.description: Small fish need small food, and raising fry often means having the right live food available at the right stage of development. The Freshwater Live Food Variety Pack – Fry and Micro Foods starts with 100+ Live Daphnia and pairs them with your choice of a second Aquatic Arts-bred live food, giving you two different feeding options in one pack. Every pack includes 100+ Live Daphnia , plus your choice of Microworms, Whiteworms, Vinegar Eels, Banana Worms, or Walter Worms . Each live food differs in size, movement, and how it is presented to fish, allowing breeders and aquarists to choose a combination that better matches the fish they are feeding. Every pack also includes a FREE 8 oz bag of Aquatic Arts Green Water Culture . Green water contains suspended microscopic algae and microorganisms that can be used as a food source when establishing or maintaining a Daphnia culture. This gives you the option of feeding the Daphnia directly, starting your own culture, or doing a little of both. This pack is especially useful for fish breeders, fry, juveniles, nano fish, small-mouthed community fish, and aquarists who want to introduce more live-food variety . Not every food in the pack is appropriate for every fry or every fish, which is why understanding the differences between them is an important part of choosing your combination. The Live Daphnia, Green Water Culture, and all five selectable live foods in this Variety Pack are Bred by Aquatic Arts . What You Receive Every Variety Pack includes: 100+ Live Daphnia – Bred by Aquatic Arts FREE 8 oz Green Water Culture – Bred by Aquatic Arts Plus your choice of one: Microworms – 2 oz – Bred by Aquatic Arts Whiteworms – 2 oz – Bred by Aquatic Arts Vinegar Eels – 10 mL culture – Bred by Aquatic Arts Banana Worms – 2 oz – Bred by Aquatic Arts Walter Worms – 2 oz – Bred by Aquatic Arts What We Love About This Live Food Variety Pack 100+ Live Daphnia: A generous portion for feeding your fish, starting a Daphnia culture, or doing a little of both. Choose a Second Live Food: Pair your Daphnia with one of five cultures based on the size and life stage of the fish you are feeding. Free Green Water Included: Every pack includes 8 oz of our Green Water Culture that can be used as a food source when establishing or maintaining Daphnia. Bred by Aquatic Arts: The Daphnia, Green Water, and every selectable live food in the pack are cultured and produced by Aquatic Arts. Why Live Daphnia? Live Daphnia move through the water column, where their swimming behavior can trigger active feeding and hunting responses from many freshwater fish. Their movement makes them particularly interesting for fish that naturally pursue small aquatic organisms rather than waiting for food to settle. Daphnia can be useful for many fry once the fish are large enough to consume the particular Daphnia being offered, as well as juveniles, nano fish, and appropriately sized adults. They should not automatically be considered a first food for every newly hatched fry because mouth size varies considerably among species. Daphnia can also be maintained and cultured by the aquarist rather than treated only as a one-time feeding. That is one reason we include our Green Water Culture with every pack. Customers interested in maintaining their Daphnia can use the Green Water as a starting food source while establishing their culture. Pairing Daphnia with a second live food gives the aquarist another feeding option with a different size, movement, and feeding behavior. Which Second Live Food Should I Choose? Microworms Microworms are tiny nematodes widely used by fish breeders as live food for fry. Their small size makes them useful for many fry that are not yet capable of taking larger live foods. Unlike Daphnia, Microworms do not remain actively swimming throughout the water column in the same way. This gives the two foods different feeding characteristics and makes the combination useful for aquarists raising fish at different stages or feeding species with different feeding behaviors. Consider Daphnia + Microworms for: breeders, fry, small juveniles, and aquarists looking for two distinctly different small live foods. Vinegar Eels Vinegar Eels are extremely small nematodes maintained in a vinegar-based culture. Their tiny size and tendency to remain suspended in the water make them particularly useful for very small fry that feed within the water column. They are harvested from their culture before being offered to fish; the vinegar culture medium itself should not be poured into the aquarium. Consider Daphnia + Vinegar Eels for: very small fry and breeders who want live foods covering distinctly different food sizes and stages of development. Banana Worms Banana Worms are very small cultured nematodes related in use to Microworms. Their small size makes them another useful option for fry and very small fish capable of consuming them. They provide breeders with another easily maintained live-food culture that can be harvested as needed. Consider Daphnia + Banana Worms for: fry, small juveniles, nano fish, and breeders maintaining multiple live-food cultures. Walter Worms Walter Worms are another small cultured nematode used as live food for fry and small fish. Their size and culture method make them useful when an aquarist wants a renewable source of tiny moving food. They can complement Daphnia by providing a much smaller food option for fish that are not yet ready for larger live foods. Consider Daphnia + Walter Worms for: fry, small fish, and breeders looking to maintain a small live-food culture alongside Daphnia. Whiteworms Whiteworms are the outlier in this pack, and that can be exactly why you choose them. They are substantially larger than Microworms, Banana Worms, Walter Worms, and Vinegar Eels . Whiteworms should therefore not be treated as a first food for tiny fry simply because they are included in a Fry and Micro Foods Variety Pack. Instead, Whiteworms can give breeders a larger live-food option for appropriately sized juveniles, adult fish, or breeding stock while Daphnia cover smaller fish and different feeding situations. Consider Daphnia + Whiteworms for: breeders feeding multiple life stages, fish rooms with different-sized fish, conditioning appropriately sized adults, or aquarists who want two substantially different live foods.

listings.commonName: Freshwater Live Food Variety Pack – Choose Your Worms, 3 Pack
listings.description: Raising fish often means feeding more than one size of food. Tiny fry, growing juveniles, breeding adults, and nano fish can have very different feeding needs, which is why maintaining several live-food cultures can be so useful. The Choose Your Worms 3 Pack lets you select any three Aquatic Arts-bred live foods from Microworms, Whiteworms, Vinegar Eels, Banana Worms, and Walter Worms. Choose three different cultures to build a live-food rotation, combine foods for different stages of development, or select multiples of the same culture when you already know what your fish need. Every selection is cultured by Aquatic Arts, giving breeders and aquarists the opportunity to feed the cultures immediately while also maintaining them at home as renewable sources of live food. What We Love About This Variety Pack Build Around Different Life Stages: Choose foods for tiny fry, growing fish, juveniles, breeding adults, or several stages at once. Choose Any Three: Mix three different cultures, double up, or choose the same food for all three selections. Maintain Renewable Live Foods: Establish your cultures at home and harvest live food as you need it. Bred by Aquatic Arts: Every selectable live food is cultured and produced by Aquatic Arts. Choose Your Three Microworms – 2 oz Banana Worms – 2 oz Walter Worms – 2 oz Whiteworms – 2 oz Vinegar Eels – 10 mL culture Choose any three. Duplicates are welcome. Build the Box Around Your Fish For very small fry, you might combine Vinegar Eels + Microworms + Walter Worms . A breeder working with fish at several stages could choose Vinegar Eels + Microworms + Whiteworms , providing very small foods for young fish and a substantially larger live food for appropriately sized juveniles or adults. If you're maintaining several batches of fry, three smaller cultures can provide both feeding variety and some backup if one culture slows down. And if you already know your fish love Whiteworms or Microworms, there is nothing stopping you from choosing that food for two or all three selections. There isn't one perfect combination because there isn't one live food that's perfect for every fish or every stage of development. That's exactly why you build this box yourself. Quick Care Guide Product Type Live Freshwater Food Cultures Pack Size Choose 3 Live Food Cultures Available Live Foods Microworms, Banana Worms, Walter Worms, Whiteworms, Vinegar Eels Microworm Portion 2 oz Banana Worm Portion 2 oz Walter Worm Portion 2 oz Whiteworm Portion 2 oz Vinegar Eel Portion 10 mL Culture Duplicates Allowed Yes – choose any selection more than once Best For Fry, juveniles, nano fish, breeding projects, conditioning, and finicky eaters Culture at Home Yes – all selections can be maintained and propagated with proper care Production Bred by Aquatic Arts The important thing with this pack is that feeding size depends on the culture selected . Vinegar Eels and the smaller nematodes can be useful for very small fish and fry, while Whiteworms are considerably larger and are better suited to appropriately sized juveniles and adults.

listings.commonName: Green Ivory Guppy (Poecilia reticulata) – Tank Bred
listings.description: The Green Ivory Guppy ( Poecilia reticulata ) is a distinctive fancy guppy variety that brings a different look to the planted aquarium or peaceful freshwater community. Like other selectively bred fancy guppies, males and females show natural differences in size, coloration, body shape, and finnage, with each individual developing its own appearance as it matures. Green Ivory Guppies are active, social livebearers that spend much of the day exploring the upper and middle portions of the aquarium. Their peaceful temperament and manageable size make them well suited to planted displays and carefully selected community aquariums, while their constant activity ensures there is almost always something happening in the tank. Our Green Ivory Guppies are Tank Bred and available as males, females, or pairs. Their approachable care requirements, lively personality, and less commonly encountered strain make them an excellent option for both longtime guppy enthusiasts and aquarists looking to add something different to a freshwater aquarium. What We Love About This Fish A less commonly encountered fancy guppy strain that offers something different for guppy enthusiasts and community aquariums. Active and social, bringing nearly constant movement to the upper and middle portions of the aquarium. Peaceful temperament makes the Green Ivory Guppy well suited to planted aquariums and carefully selected freshwater communities. Tank bred and available as males, females, or pairs for both display aquariums and hobbyists interested in breeding. Quick Care Guide Care Level: Easy. Green Ivory Guppies are hardy and adaptable when provided with stable water conditions, making them approachable for newer aquarists while remaining rewarding for experienced guppy keepers. Temperament: Peaceful. Green Ivory Guppies generally coexist well with other peaceful community species that share similar water requirements and are not prone to fin nipping. Diet: Omnivore. A varied diet combining high-quality prepared foods with appropriately sized frozen and live foods supports healthy growth, body condition, and reproduction. Source: Tank Bred. These Green Ivory Guppies have been produced in captivity rather than collected from the wild. Average Adult Size: Approximately 1.5–2.5 inches. Adult females typically grow larger and fuller-bodied than males, while males generally remain smaller. Suggested Minimum Aquarium Size: 10 gallons. Larger aquariums provide greater water stability and additional swimming space, particularly when maintaining groups or allowing a breeding population to develop. Swimming Zone: Upper to Middle Water Column. Green Ivory Guppies spend much of their time actively swimming and foraging throughout these areas of the aquarium. Activity Level: Active. Expect frequent swimming, feeding activity, social interactions, and exploration throughout the day. Social Behavior: Social. Green Ivory Guppies benefit from the presence of other compatible guppies, although males may frequently court females when both sexes are maintained together. Breeding: Livebearer. Females give birth to fully formed, free-swimming fry rather than laying eggs. Approximate Purchase Size: Approximately 1–1.5 inches. Individual size, coloration, and finnage can vary depending on age, sex, and natural development. Water Parameters Temperature: 72°–82°F (22°–28°C). Green Ivory Guppies tolerate a reasonably broad tropical temperature range, but maintaining a stable temperature is more important than routinely allowing the aquarium to fluctuate between extremes. pH: 7.0–8.2. Neutral to moderately alkaline water is well suited to Green Ivory Guppies, particularly when the aquarium maintains consistent mineral content and water chemistry. General Hardness (GH): 8–18 dGH. Guppies generally perform best in moderately hard to hard water that provides the dissolved minerals important for healthy growth and long-term condition. Carbonate Hardness (KH): 4–12 dKH. Adequate carbonate hardness helps buffer the aquarium against sudden changes in pH and contributes to a more stable environment. Clean, stable water should always take priority over chasing an exact number within these ranges. Routine partial water changes, appropriate filtration, and avoiding sudden shifts in temperature or water chemistry will help Green Ivory Guppies remain active and healthy.

listings.commonName: Blue Mosaic Guppy (Poecilia reticulata) – Tank Bred
listings.description: Species Overview The Blue Mosaic Guppy ( Poecilia reticulata ) is a selectively bred fancy guppy variety recognized for the intricate mosaic-style patterning that develops across the fins, particularly the large caudal fin of mature males. Blue coloration provides the foundation for the strain, while the branching, irregular markings characteristic of Mosaic guppies create a more complex appearance than solid-colored varieties. Males typically display the strongest coloration and most developed finnage, while females grow larger and have a fuller body shape with more restrained coloration. Like other fancy guppies, Blue Mosaic Guppies are active, social livebearers that spend much of their time swimming and foraging through the upper and middle levels of the aquarium. Our Blue Mosaic Guppies are Tank Bred and available as males, females, or pairs. They combine the elaborate appearance associated with Mosaic guppies with the active behavior, manageable size, and approachable husbandry that have made Poecilia reticulata one of the most widely kept freshwater aquarium fish. What We Love About This Fish Distinctive Mosaic Patterning: Blue Mosaic Guppies combine blue coloration with the intricate, irregular fin patterning that gives Mosaic-type guppies their name. Impressive Male Finnage: Mature males develop the larger, more elaborate caudal and dorsal fins associated with selectively bred fancy guppies. Constant Aquarium Activity: Blue Mosaic Guppies are active throughout the upper and middle water column, bringing continuous movement to planted and community aquariums. Tank-Bred Fancy Guppy: Our Blue Mosaic Guppies are Tank Bred and available as males, females, or pairs for display aquariums or breeding projects. Quick Care Guide Scientific Name: Poecilia reticulata Common Name: Blue Mosaic Guppy Source: Tank Bred Average Purchase Size: Approximately 1–1.5 inches; size varies by age and sex Adult Size: Males typically reach approximately 1.5–2 inches, while females commonly reach approximately 2–2.5 inches Care Level: Easy. Blue Mosaic Guppies are adaptable, but consistent water quality and adequate mineral content remain important for long-term health. Temperament: Peaceful. Blue Mosaic Guppies are appropriate for planted and community aquariums with non-aggressive species that thrive under similar water conditions. Diet: Omnivore. Offer a varied diet built around quality prepared foods and supplemented with appropriately sized live, frozen, and plant-based foods. Social Behavior: Social and active. Blue Mosaic Guppies interact frequently with other guppies but do not form the tightly coordinated schools characteristic of many tetras and rasboras. Males regularly display and court females. Activity Level: Active Aquarium Level: Upper to middle water column Minimum Aquarium Size: 10 gallons; larger aquariums provide greater water stability and more swimming space, particularly for groups and breeding populations. Lifespan: Approximately 2–3 years, although genetics, temperature, nutrition, reproductive demands, and overall husbandry influence individual lifespan. Aquatic Arts Tip Blue Mosaic Guppies are adaptable, but adaptable does not mean indifferent to water quality . Stable, mineral-rich water and consistent aquarium maintenance are more important than repeatedly adjusting the aquarium to chase an exact pH or hardness number. Recommended Water Parameters & Aquarium Requirements Water Parameters Temperature: 72–82°F (22–28°C) pH: 7.0–8.2 GH: 8–18 dGH KH: 4–12 dKH Ammonia: 0 ppm Nitrite: 0 ppm Nitrate: Ideally maintained below 20 ppm through appropriate stocking, feeding, filtration, and regular water changes Aquarium Requirements Minimum Aquarium Size: 10 gallons. Larger aquariums provide greater water stability and are strongly recommended for larger groups, community setups, or aquariums where fry will be allowed to grow. Filtration: Use reliable biological and mechanical filtration sized appropriately for the aquarium. Sponge filters are particularly useful in breeding setups because they provide biological filtration without creating dangerous intake suction for newborn fry. Water Flow: Low to moderate. Blue Mosaic Guppies are active swimmers but do not require strong current, and excessive flow can become unnecessarily demanding for fancy guppies with developed finnage. Oxygenation: Maintain good gas exchange through appropriate filtration, surface movement, or supplemental aeration when necessary. Aquarium Maturity: A fully cycled aquarium is required. Blue Mosaic Guppies should never be used to cycle a new aquarium. Plants: Highly recommended. Live plants provide cover, grazing surfaces, visual barriers, and refuge for fry while contributing to a more biologically active aquarium. Lighting: Low to moderate lighting is suitable for the fish themselves. Choose lighting intensity primarily around the requirements of the live plants being maintained. Aquatic Arts Tip Stability matters more than chasing a perfect number. Blue Mosaic Guppies thrive in moderately hard, mineral-rich water, but repeatedly adjusting pH or hardness can create more stress than maintaining stable conditions within an appropriate range. Test your source water, understand what comes from your tap, and build your husbandry around consistency.

listings.commonName: Purple Moscow Guppy (Poecilia reticulata) – Tank Bred
listings.description: Species Overview The Purple Moscow Guppy ( Poecilia reticulata ) is a selectively bred fancy guppy strain belonging to the Moscow group of guppies, which are recognized for extensive coloration that develops across the body and fins rather than being concentrated primarily in the tail. Purple Moscow Guppies are selected for the rich purple-toned appearance associated with this particular Moscow variety, with individual coloration naturally varying with age, sex, genetics, lighting, and condition. Males typically develop the strongest overall coloration and more elaborate finnage, while females grow larger, develop fuller bodies, and generally display more restrained coloration. Like other domestic guppies, Purple Moscow Guppies are active, social livebearers that spend much of the day swimming, displaying, and foraging through the upper and middle portions of the aquarium. Our Purple Moscow Guppies are Tank Bred and available as males, females, or pairs. Their extensive coloration, active behavior, manageable adult size, and established Moscow-type appearance make them particularly appealing for planted display aquariums as well as aquarists interested in maintaining and selectively breeding fancy guppy strains. What We Love About This Fish Classic Moscow-Type Appearance: Purple Moscow Guppies belong to the distinctive Moscow group of fancy guppies, known for extensive coloration across the body and fins. Exceptional Male Display: Mature males develop the strongest coloration and elaborate finnage, creating a striking display as they move through the aquarium. Active and Highly Visible: Purple Moscow Guppies spend much of the day swimming, foraging, and interacting throughout the upper and middle water column. Tank-Bred Fancy Guppy: Our Purple Moscow Guppies are Tank Bred and available as males, females, or pairs for display aquariums and selective breeding projects. Quick Care Guide Scientific Name: Poecilia reticulata Common Name: Purple Moscow Guppy Source: Tank Bred Average Purchase Size: Approximately 1–1.5 inches; size varies by age and sex Adult Size: Males typically reach approximately 1.5–2 inches, while females commonly reach approximately 2–2.5 inches Care Level: Easy. Purple Moscow Guppies are adaptable, but consistent water quality and adequate mineral content remain important for long-term health. Temperament: Peaceful. Purple Moscow Guppies are appropriate for planted and community aquariums with non-aggressive species that thrive under similar water conditions. Diet: Omnivore. listings.commonName: Betta Livida “Klang” (Betta livida) – Tank-Bred
listings.description: Species Overview The Betta livida “Klang” ( Betta livida ) is a rare and difficult-to-find wild betta prized by aquarists who want to experience a very different side of the genus Betta . Rather than the large flowing fins of the familiar domestic betta, Betta livida has a more natural appearance, with deep body coloration and iridescent green to blue-green markings that become especially noticeable when the fish are displaying. The “Klang” designation identifies the locality associated with this particular Betta livida line , making that information important for aquarists interested in maintaining locality-specific wild bettas. These fish should not simply be thought of as another color variety of betta. One of the most interesting characteristics of Betta livida is its social behavior. These bettas can be maintained in groups when given an appropriately sized and heavily structured aquarium with abundant cover and broken sight lines. Individuals still establish relationships and territories, so group keeping does not mean aggression is impossible. Instead, it makes aquarium structure, group composition, and observation particularly important. Aquatic Arts offers Tank-Bred and USA Bred Betta livida “Klang” when available . Because this is an uncommon species with limited availability in the aquarium hobby, it may not be something we can consistently offer throughout the year. For aquarists accustomed only to domestic bettas, Betta livida offers something completely different: a rare wild betta that can be observed interacting as a group, displaying natural social behavior, and potentially forming breeding pairs within a carefully designed aquarium. What We Love About This Fish Rare and difficult to find in the aquarium hobby, making Betta livida a special opportunity for wild betta enthusiasts Can be kept and observed in groups when provided with adequate space, dense cover, and broken sight lines Beautiful natural coloration with iridescent green to blue-green markings that become especially noticeable during displays Available as Tank-Bred and USA Bred options when available, helping support continued captive keeping of this uncommon wild betta Quick Care Guide Care Level: Moderate Temperament: Peaceful to Semi-Aggressive; Social for a Betta Adult Size: Approximately 2 to 2.5 Inches Diet: Carnivore / Micropredator (Small Pellets, Frozen Foods, and Live Foods) Minimum Tank Size: 10 Gallons for a Pair; 20+ Gallons Recommended for a Group Swimming Zone: Middle to Upper Social Behavior: Can Be Kept in Pairs or Groups With Proper Aquarium Structure Group Size: Small groups can be maintained together when given adequate space, dense planting, hiding areas, and broken sight lines. Individual behavior should always be monitored. Source: Tank-Bred / USA Bred options available when listed Scientific Name: Betta livida Locality: Klang Purchase Size: Approximately 1 to 1.5 Inches Important: A tight-fitting lid is essential. Like other wild bettas, Betta livida is capable of jumping, including through surprisingly small openings. Recommended Water Parameters Temperature: 75° to 82°F (24° to 28°C) Current Aquatic Arts pH: Approximately 7.3 Recommended Long-Term pH: Approximately 6.0 to 6.8 Breeding Target: Around pH 6.0 Wild Habitat pH: Can fall below pH 4.0 in its natural peat-swamp habitat GH: Low to Moderate KH: Low to Moderate Ammonia: 0 ppm Nitrite: 0 ppm Nitrate: Ideally below 20 ppm Our Betta livida “Klang” are captive-bred fish currently maintained at Aquatic Arts at approximately pH 7.3 . Because these fish have been raised in conditions different from the extremely acidic water sometimes recorded for wild Betta livida , there is no reason to immediately lower a newly received fish to a pH of 6.0 or below. For newly arrived fish, stable water chemistry should come first . Avoid making a sudden pH change simply to match published wild-habitat parameters. For long-term care, we recommend gradually moving toward softer, more acidic water around pH 6.0 to 6.8 . Aquarists interested in breeding Betta livida “Klang” should aim closer to pH 6.0 , along with low mineral content, gentle filtration, botanicals, and stable water quality. Wild Betta livida can inhabit remarkably acidic peat-swamp water, including environments with a pH below 4.0. That information is important for understanding the species, but wild-habitat parameters should not be confused with the conditions in which these particular captive-bred fish have been raised.

listings.commonName: Aru IV Gertrude’s Spotted Blue-Eye Rainbowfish (Pseudomugil gertrudae) – Tank-Bred
listings.description: Species Overview The Aru IV Gertrude’s Spotted Blue-Eye Rainbowfish ( Pseudomugil gertrudae ) is a small, highly active rainbowfish known for its brilliant blue eyes, translucent body, and beautifully patterned fins. Mature males are especially impressive, developing elongated fins covered in dark spots that they spread while displaying to females and competing with other males. This particular form originates from the Aru Islands population of Pseudomugil gertrudae and is commonly referred to in the aquarium hobby as Aru IV. Rather than relying on size or intense body color to stand out, these fish put on a show through constant movement and fin displays. Keeping several males together can actually make the aquarium more interesting, as they regularly posture and display without the serious aggression associated with many territorial fish. Aru IV Gertrude’s Spotted Blue-Eyes are social fish and should be kept in a group rather than individually. A larger group also allows their natural social behavior to develop while spreading attention among multiple fish. Their small adult size makes them particularly well suited to planted nano and community aquariums with other peaceful species. We offer Tank-Bred and USA Bred options when available. Both provide the same beautiful Aru IV form of Pseudomugil gertrudae , with the source clearly identified so you know which option you are purchasing. A mature aquarium with consistent water quality provides a much better environment than one where parameters fluctuate, even when those fluctuations remain within the recommended range.

listings.commonName: Purple Tiger Guppy (Poecilia reticulata) – Bred by Aquatic Arts
listings.description: Species Overview The Purple Tiger Guppy ( Poecilia reticulata ) is a selectively bred fancy guppy that combines rich purple and violet coloration with the darker striping and patterned appearance that gives the Tiger line its name. The contrast between the metallic body coloration, darker markings, and colorful fins makes each fish a little different from the next. Our team raises these fish directly, giving us firsthand experience with their development, behavior, and care rather than simply receiving finished fish from another breeder. Males typically develop the strongest coloration and more elaborate finnage, while females are generally larger and more subtly colored. Because this is a selectively bred living strain, the exact amount of purple coloration, pattern placement, and finnage will naturally vary between individuals and continue developing as younger fish mature. Purple Tiger Guppies are active, social livebearers that spend much of their time exploring the middle and upper portions of the aquarium. They readily learn feeding routines, interact constantly with other guppies, and bring plenty of movement to a planted community aquarium. Like other guppies, they are also prolific livebearers. listings.commonName: Super Blue Emperor Tetra (Inpaichthys kerri) – Tank-Bred
listings.description: Species Overview The Super Blue Emperor Tetra ( Inpaichthys kerri ) is a selectively bred form of the Blue Emperor Tetra known for its especially intense blue to violet-blue coloration . Its metallic color can shift noticeably with aquarium lighting and the angle of the fish, while a darker lateral stripe provides contrast along the body. These Tank-Bred tetras are small, active community fish that show their best behavior and appearance when maintained in a proper social group. Rather than purchasing one or two as individual display fish, keeping a group allows the Super Blue Emperor Tetra to interact naturally while creating considerably more movement and color throughout the aquarium. Males generally develop stronger blue coloration as they mature, while females tend to have a fuller body and more subdued coloration. Keeping multiple individuals also gives males opportunities to display toward one another, which can make their coloration particularly noticeable. Despite sharing the “Emperor Tetra” name, Inpaichthys kerri should not be confused with the Emperor Tetra ( Nematobrycon palmeri ) . They are separate species with different appearances, and this Super Blue form belongs to Inpaichthys kerri . For a planted community aquarium, the Super Blue Emperor Tetra offers something unusual: a small schooling fish with brilliant blue coloration that becomes even more impressive when an entire group is moving through the aquarium. listings.commonName: Green Wavy Buce Plant (Bucephalandra sp. "Green Wavy")
listings.description: This lovely buce plant has very unique, wavy leaves and is a perfect plant for the nano aquarium! Green Wavy Buce Plant ( Bucephalandra sp. “Green Wavy”) is a variant of the extremely popular Bucephalandra group. This particular Buce plant is known for its ruffled, bright green leaves. It is a very hardy plant that can be grown emersed or submerged in the aquarium, terrarium, and paludarium. It requires only low to moderate lighting and can thrive in a variety of water parameters. With proper care, Green Wavy Buce Plant will grow at a slow to moderate rate. The care of Buce plants is similar to Anubias and Cryptocoryne species. Also, like Anubias , Buce plants are rhizome plants that attach to and grow on hard surfaces. Ther attach particularly well to rocks, but can also grow very well on driftwood and other surfaces. If planted on the substrate, Buce plants should be only partially embedded in the substrate with the rhizome exposed. If the rhizome is buried, it is prone to rot. In addition to its attractive appearance, Green Wavy Buce Plant provides a valuable refuge for aquarium animals, especially dwarf shrimp, nano fish, and fry. With proper care, Green Wavy Buce Plant can easily flourish and grow to become a major centerpiece of the planted aquarium! Like most plants, Green Wavy Buce Plant will benefit from supplementation such as Seachem Flourish, Flourish Excel, Nitrogen and other plant supplements. However, supplementation is not required for this plant to grow and stay healthy. Buce plants generally show their most intense coloration and optimal growth when submerged with high lighting and stable, consistent fertilization. Drastic changes in fertilization can result in gradual leaf loss, although the plant rhizome will typically recover in time. No aquarium plant distributor/nursery/wholesaler/retailer can or will guarantee their plants to be 100% snail free. We can not guarantee our plants will be snail free. Our current specimens of this plant are small portions that have at least 4-6 leaves. What We Like About This Plant: Exceptional coloration Thrives in low-tech and high-tech setups Can be attached to almost any aquarium décor Perfect for shrimp and nano tanks Care Guidelines: Temperature: 71.6° - 82.4° F (22° - 28° C) pH: 5.0 - 8.0, although 6.0 - 7.5 is more ideal. Lighting: Low to High Origin: Indigenous to Borneo, Indonesia. Cultivated in Asian and US nurseries Aquarium placement: Middle and foreground. Rhizome should not be completely buried. Care: Easy to Moderate All Aquatic Arts brand plants and animals come with a 100% live arrival guarantee, plus free email support!

listings.description: * For the safety of our animals, we now ship live fish exclusively via UPS Next Day Air. If your order contains this item, you will only see UPS Next Day Air as a shipping option during checkout * We are proud to offer an extremely rare albino color morph or this exquisite tetra, and its incredible yellow and blue coloration are much more striking than the usual “all-pink” albino! The Albino Emperor Tetra ( Nematobrycon palmeri ) is a very attractive shoaling fish for the community aquarium. Unlike many albino color morphs, this tetra is not just the usual pink color. As it matures, both male and female specimens show canary yellow and iridescent blue coloration in addition to the characteristic “pink eye” that is typically displayed by albino specimens display. In addition, adult males have dramatically elongated dorsal and caudal fins, including an extended middle caudal ray that creates a “trident” tail. Females are generally smaller and thicker in size. The Albino Emperor Tetra typically breeds in pairs and must be kept in shoals of at least 6 to 10 fish. While juveniles will school in the typical manner of young tetras, adults are more likely to shoal and stake off their own small territories. Mature males will posture and compete for females, but this aggression is not a problem in aquariums with ample space and plenty of décor. The Albino Emperor Tetra typically occupies the top and middle level of the water column, although it can often be seen swimming and feeding in the middle and bottom levels as well. It is safe to keep with other peaceful, small fish. Though it has a relatively robust, larger body than many smaller tetras, it has a very small mouth. Adult dwarf shrimp are possibly safe tankmates as well, but adult Albino Emperor Tetras may eat small dwarf shrimp and their fry. Larger, peaceful invertebrates can also make good tankmates. Since they are tank-raised, Albino Emperor Tetras are fairly adaptable, but their natural habitat contains soft, acidic water rich in tannins and leaf litter. While not a picky eater, the Albino Emperor Tetra will thrive and remain very colorful on a varied diet of meaty foods. High-quality flake food, pellets, and frozen or freeze-dried foods will all be readily accepted.
